title: SSO session binding race causes transient role deltas and missing audit events
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A customer reported intermittent permission errors and, in one case, a temporary over-permissioned action after an SSO group sync. Root cause appears to be a race between external SAML/SCIM identity updates and our RBAC v2 in-memory session binding path. When a user's external groups change during an active session, the platform currently applies a fast-cached authority path that can either (a) refuse an action because it still sees the old, narrower role, or (b) temporarily permit an elevated action when an entry in the fast-path incorrectly merges role deltas. In addition, audit logs are missing entries for the fast-path fallback (we never emit the role_resolution_trace event in this code path).

Reproduction (observed / deterministic steps):
1) Configure customer with SAML group-to-role mapping and a live session on host A.
2) Trigger external identity update (group removal/add) via IdP SCIM change while session active.
3) Immediately trigger an API action that depends on the role change (create project / manage tokens).
4) On ~1-2% of runs, either the action is denied (server correctly uses pre-change role then rejects new action) or -- in a more concerning case -- action succeeds while audit shows incorrect role resolution or no audit event.

Key findings from investigation:
- Race window: 200ms-5s depending on GC and scheduling; correlated with heavy auth cache churn and pod restarts.
- Fast-path cache: to meet latency SLOs we maintain a session-binding cache with optimistic merging of role deltas. That merging logic had a bug when role sets were disjoint: it could create an unioned authority object for a short period before the authoritative sync completed (leading to over-permission).
- Audit gap: the cache fast-path bypassed the role_resolution_trace/emitted_audit hook on a specific code path (cacheHit && optimisticMerge) — so actions executed there have no audit entries for the role decision (audit event missing).
- SSO mapping ordering: SAML assertions don't include an explicit monotonic version for group syncs; our system used last-write timestamps which are non-deterministic under clock skew among IdP replicas.

Proposed fixes (short + long term):
- Hotfix (1-2 days): disable optimistic union-merge in the fast-path and add an audit emission for the cached-check path. This reduces the race window and ensures actions are audited. Implement a conservative fallback: if role_version unknown or last_sync_age < 10s, deny elevated actions and surface clear error to user.
- Proper fix (3 sprints): introduce role_version token propagated into session cookies / access tokens, persist authoritative role_version in user metadata, and make SSO/SCIM synces increment a deterministic version (UUID v4 with monotonic mapping in our control plane or use event-sequence id from SCIM webhooks). Serialize updates per-user to prevent interleaving updates for the same principal.
- Audit backlog reconciliation: run a one-time audit rewriter that emits synthetic role_resolution_trace events for actions in the affected time windows (only for internal investigation and compliance; mark synthetic in metadata).

Trade-offs / performance considerations:
- Disabling optimistic merges increases average auth path latency by ~3-7ms at p95, measured in benchmarks; acceptable under SLO (100ms) but must be measured on Dedicated pools.
- Adding role_version checks increases token size and slightly more DB reads for user metadata; mitigate with local TTL cache keyed by role_version.

Acceptance criteria:
- No regression in unit and integration tests for RBAC v2 (all new tests pass).
- Canary rollout shows failure rate for auth-based errors reduced to baseline and no missing audit events in the canary window.
- Customer replication attempts fail to reproduce over 500 runs after hotfix.
- Security review sign-off obtained and PRs linked.

Rollout plan:
1) Patch branch + internal QA (hotfix) -> merge to canary (10% in-hosted) -> monitor 24h.
2) If green, promote to 50% then 100% for hosted. Dedicated/private customers with strict upgrade windows will be notified; provide opt-in patch and a migration playbook.
3) Schedule full fix during next RBAC sprint with longer testing and migration for session role_version.

Links & artifacts:
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6789 (hotfix + audit hook)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/RBAC-v2+role_version+proposal
- Customer escalation: CUST-4421 (support ticket)
- Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ab12/authz-errors?orgId=1
- Postmortem template: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RBACPostmortem

Notes for support / CSE messaging:
- Communicate that a hotfix has been deployed to reduce race window and to ensure audit trail completeness. Invite customers to validate workflows and provide logs. We will follow up with a permanent fix and a timeline within 2 weeks.

implementation_tasks: Add audit hook emission for cached auth path (hotfix)
Disable optimistic union-merge in session cache and gate behind feature flag
Add conservative deny for permission increases when role_version unknown and last_sync_age < 10s
Design and implement role_version propagation into session tokens (long-term)
Implement per-user update serialization for SCIM/SAML syncs
deployment_plan: Hotfix -> canary (10%) for 24h -> 50% for 6h -> full. Use feature flag for Dedicated/private. Communicate to customers and provide opt-in where needed. Rollback strategy: revert PR and toggle feature flag to true to enable prior behavior if regression seen.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Deny-on-unknown could cause extra permission denials for users during SCIM outages. Mitigation: short window (10s), clear UI message and logs, and support playbook to re-sync user on demand. Risk: perf regression for Dedicated clusters; mitigation: run dedicated load test and consider per-customer feature flag.
postmortem_plan: After full rollout capture all affected traces, run audit backlog reconciliation for 72h window, publish postmortem with timeline, root cause, and learnings. Notify compliance for synthetic audit events.
